# Project Kestrel — Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Reviewed against:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook
**Caveat on sources:** The Seller's draft and Disclosure Letter are counterparty documents. Nothing in them is "agreed", "settled", "adequate" or "not material" merely because the Seller says so. The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026 (data-room cut-off 5.00pm); today is 4 November 2026, so every factual statement below should be refreshed before we rely on it. Where I say "assume no X", that is per playbook — not a verified fact.

---

## Summary table

| # | Issue | Seller position | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPA-N-001 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | **Reject** — hold 25% / AUD 6.0m |
| SPA-N-002 | De minimis / basket | 25k / 250k, excess-only | **Reject** — 5k / 50k, first dollar |
| SPA-N-003 | Claims period | 18 months | **Reject** — hold 24 months |
| SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | **Reject** — separate 100% / 6-yr regime |
| SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | None; limitations apply to "all Claims" | **Reject** — full carve-out, non-waivable |
| SPA-N-006 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | **Reject** — specific fair disclosure only |
| SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket exclusion incl. "discoverable" | **Reject/delete** |
| SPA-N-008 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | **Reject** — effective consent + conditions evidenced pre-Completion |
| SPA-N-009 | Riverlark | Post-completion release | **Reject** — payout, direct repayment, releases at Completion |
| SPA-N-010 | Bonuses | Seller's matter; not in funds flow | **Reject** — line item + on-costs, seller-funded |
| SPA-N-011 | Ironquay | Narrow SOW3-only indemnity "adequate" | **Reject** — broaden, keep SOW3 cure |
| SPA-N-012 | DD-006 incident | "Preliminary, not material" | **Do not accept characterisation** — preserve/investigate/update |
| SPA-N-013 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Assess** — no automatic classification either way |
| SPA-N-014 | Category separation | Limitations override all unless stated otherwise | **Reject** — express separate regimes |
| SPA-N-015 | Title | DD-012 register | **Insufficient** — independent evidence required |
| SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP | "Settled under general regime" | **Reject** — remains OPEN |

---

## Issue-by-issue

### SPA-N-001 — General liability cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% of price / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation: Reject and hold at 25% / AUD 6.0m.**
  *Reason:* 20% happens to match our conditional fallback, but no written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft has been given — a number matching a fallback does not clear it (playbook 0.4/6.3).

### SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; Seller liable from the first dollar once basket exceeded (tipping basket).
- **Recommendation: Reject on all three elements.**
  *Reason:* Seller's thresholds are 5× ours and the excess-only mechanic converts the basket into a deductible, materially eroding recovery.

### SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit (cl 12.3/13)
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months.
- **Recommendation: Reject; hold 24 months.**
  *Reason:* 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.

### SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime — 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside general basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation: Reject.**
  *Reason:* Folding title/capacity into a 20%/18-month regime would leave the core "do we own what we paid for" risk under-protected; "administrative simplicity" is not a reason.

### SPA-N-005 — Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out offered; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature".
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; not waivable by anyone.
- **Recommendation: Reject the "all Claims" formulation; insert express carve-out.**
  *Reason:* As drafted the Seller would be capped and time-barred even for its own fraud — an absolute no-go under the playbook.

### SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope (Sch 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), the Accounts, statutory registers and publicly searchable records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only (fair enough to enable a reasonable buyer to identify nature and scope); reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation: Reject paragraphs 1.1 and 1.2; require a specific disclosure schedule cross-referenced to warranties.**
  *Reason:* Whole-data-room disclosure would effectively neutralise the warranties and shift DD risk wholesale onto us.

### SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket exclusion. If any qualifier survives, it must (a) be limited to actual knowledge of named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry, and (b) never apply to title, capacity, fraud or any specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation: Delete cl 8.3.**
  *Reason:* "Discoverable" plus adviser knowledge is a constructive-knowledge bar that duplicates the deemed-disclosure problem and would gut the warranty package.

### SPA-N-008 — Bluefen change-control consent (cl 3/6.3)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms **no final written consent and no evidence conditions under cl 11.3 are satisfied** as at 22 Sept 2026.
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring effective consent **and** evidence that all conditions (DD-002 cl 11.3) are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; endeavours standard escalated (all reasonable/best endeavours with specified actions).
- **Recommendation: Reject; redraft as a hard CP with conditions-evidence requirement.**
  *Reason:* Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m); a consent that is "delivered" but conditional is not a consent.
- **Action:** Request current status — has anything moved since 22 September?

### SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility (cl 2/7)
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to be provided after Completion. Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms **not repaid, no final discharge** in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases/discharges delivered at Completion. Any post-completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark plus Amelia Frost approval.
- **Recommendation: Reject post-completion release.**
  *Reason:* Debt-free/cash-free pricing is meaningless if AUD 3.2m of secured debt and change-of-control (cl 8.1) exposure sits in the Company on Day 1.
- **Action:** Obtain updated payout figure (22 Sept figure is stale).

### SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses (DD-005; funds flow)
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 Completion bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in funds flow. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are absent and is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus all triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals if applicable) as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly Seller-funded / treated as Debt-like item; funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation: Reject; require line item and Seller funding of gross cost.**
  *Reason:* "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the Company (i.e. us) pays it post-Completion.
- **Action:** Ask Seller to quantify on-costs.

### SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity (cl 11.1; DD-004/DD-010)
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter para 4: AUD 180,000 open per DD-010 (not independently verified); no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broadened indemnity covering ownership/transfer of all Ironquay Project Materials, third-party claims and remediation cost, while preserving the SOW3 cure (pay the fee → trigger cl 7.3 transfer); require confirmatory assignment at Completion.
- **Recommendation: Reject "adequate"; broaden.**
  *Reason:* Under cl 7.3 title to SOW3 materials does not pass until every fee is cleared, so the IP risk is wider than a single AUD 180k payment — which itself is unverified in either direction.
- **Action:** Seek bank evidence of payment status and a confirmatory IP assignment.

### SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6; DD-006)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter para 6: ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps) sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined; investigation preliminary; no loss stated.
- **Buyer wants:** Litigation/forensic hold on logs; completed investigation with written findings; ongoing update covenant to Completion; specific indemnity for pre-Completion incident costs; no acceptance of "not material".
- **Recommendation: Do not accept the Seller's characterisation; impose preserve / investigate / update obligations.**
  *Reason:* Per playbook, assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or quantum — but equally none of those can be ruled out on a six-week-old "preliminary" record.
- **Action:** Request current investigation status (what has happened since 22 September?).

### SPA-N-013 — Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008/DD-011)
- **Seller:** 3 × AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000 are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8 admits it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:** Facts — timing, termination rights, whether accrued pre-Completion, whether committed ahead of need.
- **Recommendation: Assess; neither accept "ordinary course" nor assert Debt classification or price deduction yet.**
  *Reason:* The Seller's own letter concedes it has not established the facts that would support its "ordinary course" label.

### SPA-N-014 — Category separation (cl 12.3/13; 9.3/12.8/20.5)
- **Seller:** Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise; limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment/leakage and covenant claims each expressly in separate regimes; no general-regime override by default.
- **Recommendation: Reject the default-override language; invert it so general limitations apply **only** to General Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.**
  *Reason:* This clause is the mechanism by which SPA-N-004, 005, 011 and 016 would all be quietly collapsed into the 20%/18-month regime.

### SPA-N-015 — Title verification (DD-012)
- **Seller:** Title to 100% evidenced by the Company share register. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes this is the Seller's own source and does not claim Buyer verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence — ASIC searches, PPSR searches against Seller and Company, review of constitution and any shareholder/option/convertible instruments, director/shareholder authority resolutions, encumbrance confirmations and Riverlark security position (ties to SPA-N-009).
- **Recommendation: Treat DD-012 as insufficient; complete independent title DD before signing.**
  *Reason:* An internal register maintained by the Seller is a supplied source, not independent proof of unencumbered ownership or authority.

### SPA-N-016 — Tax / IP terms
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, 18 months, 25k/250k thresholds).
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; separate Tax indemnity and IP warranties with their own cap/period to be negotiated (no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed).
- **Recommendation: Reject "settled"; record Tax/IP as open in the issues list.**
  *Reason:* A counterparty cannot declare a term settled unilaterally, and nothing in our authority process has closed these points.

---

## Overarching observations

1. **Structural pattern:** The draft combines (a) low cap, (b) deductible basket, (c) short period, (d) whole-data-room disclosure, (e) constructive-knowledge bar and (f) "all Claims" override. Each alone is aggressive; together they make the warranty package close to illusory. Our mark-up should fix the architecture (SPA-N-005/006/007/014) first — the numbers (001–003) matter little if the structural clauses stand.
2. **Authority:** Two Seller numbers (20% cap, 18 months) match our fallbacks. **Neither is cleared.** No approval from Amelia Frost has been given; do not signal flexibility on either without it.
3. **Stale facts:** All disclosures speak as at 22 September 2026. Before responding, refresh Bluefen status, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment status, DD-006 investigation, and bonus on-cost quantum, and distinguish verified updates from Seller assertions.
4. **Disclosure Letter para 11** itself tells us the Buyer must evaluate facts against the full agreement and current DD — take that invitation literally.

Let me know if you want this converted into a clause-by-clause mark-up or an issues list for circulation to the deal team.
=== END ADVICE ===
